text:
Jordan: Heads-up — customer on Dedicated is seeing consistent SSE disconnects when clients sit behind a corporate proxy + VPC MTU 1400. Partial chunks arrive, then client reconnects and sometimes gets duplicate tokens. Customer says it started after they moved to our private ingress node.

Jordan: Repro summary I got from them:
- Model: open-llama-13b-v2 (we're serving quantized variant)
- Request: streaming completion via SSE, ~1200 tokens per request on average
- Network: customer internal corp proxy (windows boxes), VPC subnet with MTU 1400, egress via NAT gateway
- Client behavior: browser JS EventSource + a reconnect backoff that retries immediately on close, then sometimes shows duplicate final tokens on resume

Jordan: Attaching small snippet they sent (they said they couldn't post logs here):
```
# client side pseudo
const es = new EventSource(url);
es.onmessage = (e) => { appendChunk(e.data); }
es.onerror = () => { es.close(); startImmediateReconnect(); }
```

Sam: :eyes: thanks Jordan. A few questions to narrow down:
1) Do they see TCP FIN/RST on the server side or is the connection staying established and only SSE frames stopping?
2) Any proxy logs showing chunk splitting or 502s?
3) Is keepalive enabled between client-proxy and proxy-ingress?

Jordan: They collected tcpdump at the ingress and shared hex slice: fragmentation boundary always at 1460-ish then 940 bytes (MTU-driven), so looks like chunk boundaries coincide with MTU fragmentation. Server side logs show no error — runtime happily sending. Proxy logs show lots of keepalive timeouts ~ 60s and occasional 502s. Customer reports they have a corporate proxy that rewrites some headers.

Alex: That smells like proxy buffering + MTU causing SSE chunks to be split into weird frames and the corporate proxy isn't streaming chunked bodies well. Corporate proxies often buffer until they see a full chunk or a timeout, then close. With SSE we depend on small flushes. If their proxy reassembles and then drops partial frames when it hits its own timeout, client sees a sudden disconnect.

Alex: Quick mitigation to ask customer to try: set MTU to 1500 temporarily on their VPC host, or bypass proxy for a test (if that's possible) to confirm. Also ask them to turn on TCP keepalives on the proxy and increase proxy response timeout. If bypassing fixes it, it's proxy behavior.

Jordan: They tried bypassing the corp proxy for one client machine and said streaming was stable for ~30m. When they switched back to the proxyed path, disconnects resumed.

Sam: Good repro then. Two follow-ups from runtime side:
- We should confirm kernel-level PMTU or path MTU discovery isn't being blocked by their network (DF bit issues).
- Consider a server-side change to emit slightly larger SSE heartbeats (periodic ":\n" comments) to keep proxy streaming behavior happy.

Sam: Also want to log a small controlled experiment to see if chunk boundary alignment impacts client parsing. Jordan — can you ask customer to run this curl test from a proxyed host and paste results?

Jordan: Sent instructions to customer:
```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=open-llama-13b-v2"
```
They returned server output that shows lines ending in "\n\n" but tcpdump shows MSS splits. They also pasted a proxy error: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header` from their corp proxy.

Maria: I'm on the thread for customer comms — they care about duplicates and billing implications (they saw duplicate token counts once). We should confirm whether duplicate retry tokens were billed twice; if yes, need to propose a compensation path.

Sam: On the billing point — duplicate SSE resume tokens are likely causing the client to replay and get billed. We should check request ids in our access logs; we can probably map repeated final chunk token counts to duplicate invoice lines. Jordan, can you request logs with `x-request-id` values for the failed streams?

Jordan: Done — customer sent a compressed log excerpt with headers including `x-request-id: req_33b4a`. I matched two requests from that id within 3s of each other. Looks like client retried immediately after disconnect and server accepted second request fully (billing counted both).

Alex: Two engineering mitigations we can pursue:
- Short term: document recommended proxy settings (turn off buffering, proxy_request_buffering off for nginx, increase timeouts, pass-through chunked).
- Medium: server-side: emit SSE comments every 15s and add a small unique stream checksum on final event so client can detect duplicates and avoid billing retries.

Sam: For the runtime change: we can push a quick tweak to staging that increases our SSE keepalive comment frequency and adds a final-event checksum header. I can open a PR.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: streaming-keepalive-bump to staging.

Sam: PR opened — small change toggled by feature flag. Jordan, can we coordinate a staging test with the customer's proxy team?

Jordan: Customer agreed to try staging URL behind their proxy tomorrow morning. I'll be there for the call.

Alex: In parallel, I'll draft a KB snippet for support:
- Why SSE can break behind buffers/MTU mismatches
- Nginx tuning: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_busy_buffers_size 64k; proxy_buffers 8 64k; proxy_request_buffering off;`
- Keepalives/timeouts recommended (client->proxy 300s, proxy->ingress 180s) and enable `proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;`

Jordan: Customer asked if we can detect these nodes automatically and apply a margin; they want our platform to fall back to non-streaming responses if proxy path is flaky.

Sam: We can add a per-customer routing policy to disable streaming for requests that fail N times in T window. Let's not auto-disable globally, but we can offer it as a support toggle for Dedicated customers. I'll add a task to the runtime backlog.

Maria: For the customer-facing ticket: I drafted message clarifying causes, the staging test plan, and compensation approach if repeated duplicate billable tokens are found. Jordan — I'll send once we confirm staging test.

oncall-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-042; severity low; assignees: Sam, Alex; status: investigating.

Jordan: Follow-up from customer's proxy team during the call: they found a middlebox that enforces a 60s idle window and will reset connections that have only partial chunked frames. They will try setting `proxy_buffering off` and increasing the idle window.

Sam: Great. After they test staging, please pull server-side pcap and runtime send buffers so we can correlate. If the staging keepalive fix works we can prod to prod behind feature flag.

Jordan: After the test: streaming stable for 2h on staging, no duplicates seen. Customer will roll to prod tomorrow with the proxy changes.

Sam: Closing loop: I'll leave the feature flag on for 48h and monitor error rates and token duplication metrics. If stable, we'll schedule a controlled rollout.

Jordan: Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket and ask for final confirmation on billing if any duplicate invoices appeared. :thumbsup:
